claims.text: Builds new blood vessels to speed healing (angiogenesis).
claims.note: Rat and cell studies show increased blood vessel growth around injuries. No human study has measured it.

refs.label: Seiwerth et al., review of BPC-157 in wound healing (animal data)

claims.text: Rebuilds tendon, bone and skin stronger than before.
claims.note: Tendon and ligament repair is well documented in rats. "Stronger than before" has no support in any species.

refs.label: Chang et al. 2011, tendon fibroblast outgrowth (rat cells)

claims.text: Crosses the blood-brain barrier and acts as "neurological rehab".
claims.note: Brain effects come from rodent models. There is no human neurological data.

claims.text: Research shows BPC-157 can be anti-tumor.
claims.note: This rests on a few cell and rodent studies. Because BPC-157 promotes blood vessel growth, some researchers raise the opposite concern. Neither direction has been tested in people.

claims.text: The cancer fear is based on flawed logic.
claims.note: This is an argument, not a finding. Long-term human safety data does not exist, so neither side is settled.

claims.text: Context the infographic leaves out: regulatory status.
claims.note: BPC-157 is not FDA approved. FDA has flagged it as a compounding substance with safety concerns, and WADA bans it in sport. Human evidence is limited to small uncontrolled reports.

refs.label: FDA bulk drug substances list, Category 2 (2023)

entries.title: Retatrutide: a tactical manual for fat loss

claims.text: Activates three receptors (GLP-1, GIP, glucagon) to suppress hunger and increase fat burning.
claims.note: That is the drug's designed mechanism, and randomized trials confirm large appetite and weight effects.

claims.text: Average body weight loss of 24%+, beating semaglutide (10-15%) and tirzepatide (~20%).
claims.note: In the phase 2 trial, the top dose (12 mg) produced a 24.2% mean loss at 48 weeks. The comparison crosses separate trials with different lengths and populations, so treat it as directional.

refs.label: SURMOUNT-1, NEJM 2022 (tirzepatide up to 20.9% at 72 wks)

claims.note: This is not the trial schedule. Trials escalated toward 4, 8 and 12 mg under medical supervision. These doses come from the online community, and retatrutide is still investigational and not approved.

refs.label: Jastreboff et al., NEJM 2023, dosing arms

claims.text: When you cut calories, your body raises hunger hormones and lowers energy to defend fat stores.
claims.note: Metabolic adaptation and higher ghrelin after weight loss are well replicated in human studies.

claims.text: Calorie ceiling = body weight (lb) x 12; protein floor = 1 g per lb.
claims.note: These are coaching rules of thumb, not outputs of a trial. Protein targets around 0.7 to 1 g per lb are common in sports nutrition.

entries.title: Your TRT timeline: the first 10 weeks

claims.text: Weeks 1-4: boosts in mood, confidence, cognition and sex drive.
claims.note: In hypogonadal men, sexual interest improves around week 3 and mood around weeks 3 to 6. Cognitive effects are inconsistent across trials.

refs.label: Saad et al., Eur J Endocrinol 2011

claims.note: Lean mass gain and fat loss become measurable around 12 to 16 weeks and keep improving for months.

refs.label: Saad et al., Eur J Endocrinol 2011

claims.text: Libido is not erection quality: TRT raises desire, but erections depend on blood flow.
claims.note: Randomized trials show clear gains in desire and only modest gains in erectile function.

claims.text: Some benefits, like bone density, take a year.
claims.note: Bone density changes show up after about 6 months and keep building for years.

refs.label: Snyder et al., JAMA Intern Med 2017 (bone trial)

claims.text: Context the infographic leaves out: who TRT is for.
claims.note: These timelines come from men with confirmed low testosterone. TRT also suppresses sperm production, which matters for anyone planning children.
